engine.meaning: Facts survive (sold to the White Sox, the old man's speech, the Grand Rapids series, Flynn's misjudged fly ball), but "one of the young fellas told me" changes "the boys" (his teammates), and the swears tilt lines: "I will make bloody good".
engine.sense: "skiting" for boasting and "sweet bugger-all on you" fit; "there won't be bugger all to it" strains the sense of "there won't be nothing to it" (easy), and "make bloody good" breaks the set phrase "make good".
engine.authenticity: Swears bolted onto otherwise untouched prose: "all you bloody good old pals down home", "this bloody big league business". "Al old mate" and "beaut old times" sit oddly beside the unchanged "good old pals".
engine.register: Mostly the original with a handful of swaps ("old bloke", "skiting", "spooked", "dunno") and dense swearing: three "bloody" and two "bugger". Within vulgarity 1, but light on Aussie and heavy on swears for level 3.
engine.tone: Jack's naive boastfulness mostly comes through, but the swearing makes the cheerful letter coarser: "I will make bloody good".
engine.flow: Readable, with clunks where swears are inserted: "all you bloody good old pals down home".
engine.variety: Leans on "bloody" and "bugger": "bugger all to it", "sweet bugger-all on you", "bloody good", "bloody big league".
engine.essence: The voice, misspellings and shape are kept because most of it is the original: "I beat them twice in that serious."

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point is kept, from "I been sold to the White Sox" to "they excepted it" and "tell them I'm still their mate"; nothing invented.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Each term carries its sense: "on the cards" for coming off, "easy as" for nothing to it, "never had a hope against me when I was on song", "having a squiz at me", "not getting up myself" for not swelled up.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian writing home: "I'll be happy as Larry", "I'm not skiting when I say that Al", "Say g'day to all the boys". The misspellings are kept, so it stays Jack's voice.
yarn-dinkum.register: Squarely level 3: steady natural slang, one "sweet bugger-all", within vulgarity 1.
yarn-dinkum.tone: The proud, naive, chatty tone comes through whole: "But I reckon I seen enough of life not to get spooked by a few tall buildings, ay Al?"
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like a letter written that way: "Anyway Doyle liked what he seen and he wired Comiskey to buy me."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied; "He goes" is used three times for the old man's speech, the only noticeable repeat.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably Jack's letter, misspellings and all: "I beat them twice in that serious."

yarn-troppo.meaning: All the original points survive, with many added asides; most react to the original ("Walsh, Al! Not a bad wrap, ay?", "Wasn't my fault, Al."), but some add detail: "show them city fellas", "watching me the whole time Grand Rapids was in town".
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "like a stunned mullet", "a bit of ticker", "easy as", "on song", "No skin off my nose.", "getting up meself".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural idiom, but the asides pile on and some feel tacked: "Just telling it how it is.", "They're only buildings.", "Not one bit."
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3: the slang is thick ("stunned mullet", "ticker", "Sneaky bugger.", "No skin off my nose.") and the letter grows a running commentary. Swearing within vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: Keeps Jack's naive bragging and arguably sharpens it: "We're finishing second and I done most of it, if I say so meself." The extra tags make it more knowing than the original's deadpan.
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively, but the short tag sentences stack up: "No skin off my nose.", "Not one bit.", "Just like that, Al."
yarn-troppo.variety: Leans on one device, a short tag sentence after a line: "Just like that, Al.", "They're only buildings.", "Not one bit.", "Wasn't my fault, Al."
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably Jack's letter, but the asides change its shape from unselfconscious to winking: "Now get this."

yarn-deadset.meaning: Everything is kept, nearly line for line: "Doyle liked my work and he wired Comiskey to buy me".
yarn-deadset.sense: The few swaps fit: "it'll be easy as", "sweet bugger-all on you", "not skiting", "happy as Larry", "not all up myself".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: What Aussie there is sounds natural, "I reckon I seen enough of life not to be spooked by the high buildings eh Al?", though "eh" is left where "ay" would be local.
yarn-deadset.register: Light for level 3: most of the letter is the original, with a scatter of swaps ("old mate", "fellas", "dunno", "beaut old times").
yarn-deadset.tone: Tone kept whole: "I will just give them what I got and if they don't like it they can send me back to the old Central and I will be happy as Larry."
yarn-deadset.flow: Reads smoothly; the swaps sit in cleanly: "show those fellas that there is a Central League on the map".
yarn-deadset.variety: Each term appears once: "easy as", "skiting", "spooked", "happy as Larry", "beaut".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the original, voice and misspellings intact: "Comiskey come back with an offer and they excepted it."

unharnessed.meaning: All points kept: "Doyle liked my work and he wired Comiskey to buy me", "they excepted it". The salutation "MATE AL:" changes the original's "FRIEND AL:" heading.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "big-noting meself" for boasting, "running the eye over me", "having a squiz at me", "on song", "on the cards", "guts" for nerve.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural Australian idiom throughout ("I'm not big-noting meself", "They always done right by me here"), though "MATE AL:" as a letter heading is not how anyone writes.
unharnessed.register: Level 3 throughout: steady slang, no swearing (within vulgarity 1).
unharnessed.tone: Jack's naive pride comes through whole: "believe me Al I'll make good".
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "I didn't know nobody was running the eye over me, but one of the boys told me".
unharnessed.variety: Varied, with distinct terms for each idea: "running the eye over", "having a squiz", "big-noting", "happy as Larry", "up meself".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably Jack's letter: "I beat them twice in that serious."

engine.quote: all you bloody good old pals down home
engine.original: all you good old pals down home
engine.why: "bloody" dropped in as filler; one representative quote for the swearing bolted on through the letter.

engine.quote: there won't be bugger all to it
engine.original: there won't be nothing to it
engine.why: Strains the sense: "bugger all to it" can read as nothing in it, not that it will be easy.
Breaks the idiom "make good"; an Australian would wince.

engine.quote: one of the young fellas told me
engine.original: one of the boys told me
engine.why: "the boys" are his teammates; "young fellas" shifts who told him.

yarn-dinkum.quote: He goes Just pitch the ball you been pitching down here
yarn-dinkum.original: He says Go and pitch the ball you been pitching down here
yarn-dinkum.why: "He goes" three times in a row reads as a tic.

yarn-troppo.quote: show them city fellas there's a Central League on the map
yarn-troppo.original: show those birds that there is a Central League on the map
yarn-troppo.why: "city" is added; the original's birds are just big-leaguers.

yarn-troppo.quote: Just telling it how it is.
yarn-troppo.why: One of many tag sentences that render nothing; the pattern is a tic.
Added aside; "rap" is the usual spelling for praise.

yarn-deadset.quote: I didn't have no idea that anything like that was coming off.
yarn-deadset.original: I didn't have no idea that anything like that was coming off.
yarn-deadset.why: Much of the letter is left unchanged, so the brief's weight is not met.

unharnessed.why: A letter heading is not slangified this way; it reads as forced.

summaries.engine: Largely untranslated with swears scattered in; some breaks of sense.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: A natural, faithful level 3 that keeps Jack's voice; the best balance of the set.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and idiomatic, but over-embellished for level 3, with a tag-sentence tic.
summaries.yarn-deadset: Faithful and natural but light for level 3.
summaries.unharnessed: Natural, well-pitched and varied; only the forced salutation jars.
